title: Summary and review exercise
competency: Bring together the ideas of Unit 1.

keywords.def: Finding the size of a quantity by comparing it with an agreed standard.
A quantity that cannot be expressed in terms of any other quantity, like length, mass, time and temperature.
A quantity that depends on one or more fundamental quantities, like area, volume, speed and density.
How close a measurement is to its accepted or known value.
How close two or more measurements are to each other.
The process by which scientists approach their work: question, research, hypothesis, test, conclude, communicate.

en.text: Measurement compares a quantity with an agreed standard. Fundamental quantities (length, mass, time, temperature) give derived ones (area, volume, speed, density). Prefixes shorten big and small numbers. Accuracy is closeness to the true value; precision is agreement. The scientific method has six steps.

screens.title: Summary
paras: Measurement obtains the size of a quantity relative to an agreed standard.
Indigenous units: cubit, span, digit, foot and pace for length; weqet and quntal for mass; a shadow for time.
Fundamental quantities cannot be expressed by other quantities; derived ones combine them.
Prefixes are a short-hand for very large or very small numbers.

screens.text: Unit 1 key words: match each word with its meaning.
pairs: Short-hand for big or small numbers
screens.why:
Prefix: a short-hand for big or small numbers, like kilo.
Hypothesis: a testable explanation, step 3 of the method.
Derived quantity: built from fundamental quantities.
Cubit: elbow to middle fingertip, an indigenous unit of length.
screens.clue: One is a unit of length, one is a step of the method.

screens.ask: Convert kilometres to metres: 0.6 km = ___ m
screens.why:
1 km = 1000 m.
Big unit to small unit: multiply.
0.6 × 1000 = 600.
So 0.6 km = 600 m.

screens.text: Instruments: a thermometer is used to measure
screens.why:
Thermo- means heat.
A thermometer measures temperature, like a fever of 38.5°C.
Mass needs a balance, length a ruler, time a clock.

screens.text: Units, true or false: derived units do not depend on any other unit.
screens.why:
Derived units are built from fundamental units.
Example: m/s is built from metres and seconds.
So derived units DO depend on other units.
The statement describes fundamental units. So it is false.
screens.clue: Which kind is built from others?

screens.title: Indigenous or SI?
screens.text: Units review: sort each unit as indigenous or SI.
items: A mug used in the market.
screens.why:
Indigenous units are local and traditional: cubit, feresula, kubaya.
SI units are used by scientists everywhere: kilogram, second, metre.
SI units are the same for everyone; indigenous units can vary.
screens.clue: Would a scientist in any country use it?

screens.text: Accuracy and precision: a shop scale gives 1.05, 1.05 and 1.05 kg for a 1.00 kg standard mass. What should the shopkeeper do?
opts: Reset (calibrate) the scale: it is precise but not accurate
screens.ans: Reset (calibrate) the scale: it is precise but not accurate
screens.why:
The three readings are the same: precise.
They are 1.05 − 1.00 = 0.05 kg too high: not accurate.
The scale has the same error every time.
Resetting (calibrating) the scale fixes the accuracy.
screens.clue: Are the readings the same? Are they correct?

items.text: Fundamental quantities: which one is fundamental?
items.why:
Fundamental quantities stand alone: length, mass, time, temperature.
Temperature is one of them.
Area = length × width: derived.
Volume and force are also built from others.
So the answer is temperature.

items.text: Units: what is the difference between fundamental and derived units?
opts: Derived units are derived from fundamental units
Fundamental units come from derived units
items.ans: Derived units are derived from fundamental units
items.why:
Fundamental units stand alone: m, kg, s, K.
Derived units are built from them: m², m/s, kg/m³.
So derived units are derived from fundamental units.
Not the other way round.

items.ask: Kinds of quantity: length, mass, time and temperature are ___ quantities
items.why:
Length, mass, time and temperature are not made from other quantities.
Such quantities are fundamental (base) quantities.
So the answer is fundamental.

items.ask: Kinds of quantity: area, volume, density and force are ___ quantities
items.why:
Area = length × width.
Volume = length × width × height.
Density = mass ÷ volume. Force = mass × acceleration.
Each is built from other quantities, so they are derived.

items.text: SI units: match each quantity with its unit.
items.why:
Mass is fundamental: kilogram, kg.
Temperature is fundamental: kelvin, K.
Area = m × m = m².
Volume = m × m × m = m³.
Density = kg ÷ m³ = kg/m³.
items.clue: Square for area, cubic for volume.

items.ask: Convert metres to millimetres: 0.005 m = ___ mm
Convert centimetres to kilometres: 1000 cm = ___ km

items.text: Accuracy and precision: g = 9.81 m/s². Results of 12.2, 12.3, 12.1 and 12.08 m/s² are
items.why:
Compare the results with each other: 12.08 to 12.3, close together. Precise.
Compare them with the true value, 9.81.
They are more than 2 m/s² too high. Not accurate.
So they are precise but not accurate.

items.text: Derived quantities: which one is derived?
items.why:
A derived quantity is built from others.
Area = length × width.
So area is derived.
Mass, time and length are fundamental.

1/1000 is one thousandth = 0.001.
Milli means a thousandth: 1 mm = 0.001 m.
Kilo means 1000, the opposite.
So the answer is milli.

items.text: Derived units: the SI unit of density is
items.why:
Density = mass ÷ volume.
Mass is in kg; volume is in m³.
kg ÷ m³ = kg/m³.
kg/m² would be mass per area.

items.ask: Convert centimetres to metres: one million centimetres = ___ m
items.why:
One million = 1 000 000.
100 cm = 1 m, so divide by 100.
1 000 000 ÷ 100 = 10 000.
So one million cm = 10 000 m.

items.text: Scientific method: put the six steps in order.
items.why:
1 Ask questions.
2 Do background research.
3 Make a hypothesis.
4 Test it.
5 Analyse the results and conclude.
6 Communicate the results.

items.text: Indigenous units: weqet is used to measure
items.why:
Weqet is an indigenous unit of mass.
In local markets it is used for gold powder.
Grain is sold by the quntal; pepper and coffee by the feresula.
So weqet measures gold powder.

test.text: SI units: the SI unit of mass is
test.why:
Mass is a fundamental quantity.
Its SI unit is the kilogram (kg).
Gram and tonne are other units; quntal is indigenous.
So the answer is kilogram.

test.ask: Convert kilometres to metres: 5.5 km = ___ m

test.text: Accuracy and precision: darts that are all in the bullseye, close together, are
test.why:
Close together: the throws agree, so precise.
In the bullseye: they hit the target, so accurate.
So they are accurate and precise.

test.text: Fair test: changing only one factor in an experiment makes it
test.why:
If only one factor changes, any difference comes from it.
This is called a fair test.
A hypothesis is an explanation, not a way of testing.
So the answer is a fair test.

test.text: Indigenous or SI: which is NOT an indigenous unit?
test.why:
Cubit is a body unit of length: indigenous.
Quntal is a bag of grain: indigenous.
Sini is a small cup: indigenous.
Kelvin is the SI unit of temperature. So kelvin is NOT indigenous.
